profile.reading: LightEdge SAN1 sits in San Diego, California, though LightEdge own site publishes two distinct San Diego addresses, 9305 Lightwave Avenue in the 92123 zip code and 9725 Scranton Road in the 92121 zip code, on different streets and in different parts of the city, and no source reviewed this session could confirm which specific address corresponds to this record SAN1 designation. Per LightEdge own combined specification sheet for the San Diego market, the facility or facilities together provide 2.9 megawatts of critical IT load and 10 megawatts of generator capacity with N plus 1 UPS redundancy, across 100,000 total square feet including 56,342 square feet of white space. The facility carries a broad compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS, with thirteen on-net carriers including AT&T, Cogent, Comcast, Lumen, NTT, Verizon, and Zayo. LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. LightEdge announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm that also created Digital Realty in 2004, in September 2021, with then-CEO Jim Masterson stating no changes to management, operations, or customer teams as a result. Masterson led the company for 21 years before transitioning to an advisory board role effective the end of 2024, succeeded as CEO by Rob Carter on January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets plus a location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named for this facility, and no year-built or tier-rating figure is disclosed for the San Diego market on LightEdge own site. San Diego has grown as a secondary California data center market drawing enterprise and cloud customers seeking an alternative to the more expensive and power-constrained Silicon Valley market, a pattern consistent with LightEdge broader compliance-focused, mid-market business strategy across its twelve metro footprint.

reading.body:
LightEdge SAN1 publishes 2.9 megawatts of critical IT load across 56,342 square feet of white space in the San Diego market, though LightEdge's own website lists two distinct San Diego addresses on different streets and the operator has not confirmed which corresponds to this facility code. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 2.9 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 73 racks, placing this facility well below the scale required for frontier AI training clusters. The site carries SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS certifications, qualifying it for enterprise and regulated workloads rather than hyperscale compute.

San Diego has emerged as a secondary California market for enterprise and cloud tenants seeking alternatives to Silicon Valley's cost and power constraints, and LightEdge's compliance-focused portfolio across twelve US metros aligns with this mid-market positioning. Within California's 365 published megawatts of data center capacity across eleven facilities that disclose figures, LightEdge SAN1 ranks twelfth at 2.9 megawatts, accounting for less than one percent of the state's published capacity. The campus does not qualify as a binding constraint on California's grid or a material factor in AI compute scaling.

The operator does not publish a tier rating, year built, or specific power availability roadmap for this facility. No tenant is named, and the generator capacity of 10 megawatts is declared for the San Diego market at large rather than for this specific site. Without confirmation of street address, year of construction, or upgradeability trajectory, LightEdge SAN1 cannot be assessed as a growth vector in the California data center market.
